flags: Miller Industries, Inc. acquired Omars – S.p.A, a towing and recovery vehicle designer and manufacturer headquartered in Cuneo, Italy, and finalized its purchase price allocation in the third quarter of 2026.
As part of a comprehensive cost reduction plan, the Company reduced its headcount by approximately 150 positions across U.S. manufacturing facilities.
The Company offered a voluntary enhanced retirement program to U.S. employees aged 65 and above, resulting in a net financial impact of $2.7 million.
no_value_reason: some filed figures are years older than the latest annual report

business_model.claim: Miller Industries designs and manufactures bodies for car carriers and wreckers installed on third-party chassis, as well as specialized multi-vehicle transport trailers.
quotes: We design and manufacture bodies of car carriers and wreckers, which are installed on chassis manufactured by third parties, and sold to our customers.
Our multi-vehicle transport trailers are specialized auto transport trailers with upper and lower decks and hydraulic ramps for loading vehicles.

business_model.claim: The company manufactures and markets its car carriers, wreckers, and trailers under 11 separate brand names.
quotes: We manufacture and market our car carriers, wreckers, and trailers under 11 separate brand names.

business_model.claim: Miller Industries sells its products primarily through a network of approximately 76 distributor locations in North America and over 30 distributors in other foreign markets, which then sell to end-users.
quotes: We sell our products to a diverse network of independent distributors, consisting of approximately 76 distributor locations in North America, that serve all 50 states, Canada and Mexico, and over 30 distributors that serve other foreign markets.
These distributors then sell our products to end-users.

business_model.claim: The company also sells products to U.S. and foreign governmental entities through prime contractors, and reported military commitments exceeding $200 million.
quotes: In addition to providing services to our network of independent distributors, our sales representatives sell our products to various governmental entities, including the U.S. federal government and foreign governments, through prime contractors.
Military commitments currently exceed $200 million, and additional global RFQs are underway.

business_model.claim: No single distributor accounted for more than 10% of consolidated total sales in 2025, and management does not consider the business materially dependent on any single customer.
quotes: In 2025, no distributor accounted for more than 10% of our consolidated total sales and we do not consider our business to be materially dependent on any single customer.

business_model.claim: Miller Industries operates as a single reportable segment, with management evaluating performance on a consolidated basis.
quotes: Miller Industries operates as a single reportable segment and management evaluates performance on a consolidated basis.

business_model.claim: Consolidated net sales were $790.3 million in 2025, of which $148.9 million were net foreign sales occurring primarily in Europe.
quotes: Historically, a portion of our net sales occur outside the United States, primarily in Europe.
Consolidated net sales in fiscal 2025 were $790.3 million compared to $1.26 billion in fiscal 2024, a decrease of 37.2%.
Net foreign sales in fiscal 2025 were $148.9 million compared to $125.7 million in fiscal 2024, an increase of 18.5%.

business_model.basis: stated in P1, P3, and P6
business_model.claim: The company produces virtually all products to order, so revenue moves with order intake, production levels, and distributor channel inventory—2025 net sales fell 37.2% as production was lowered to reduce field inventory, while third-quarter 2026 revenue rose 18.8% to $212.2 million on steady order intake.
quotes: We produce virtually all of our products to order.
The decrease in net sales was primarily driven by lower production levels to mitigate inventory buildup in our distribution channel.
Delivered solid year-over-year revenue growth as the Company maintained production in line with steady order intake in a dynamic environment.
Revenue: $212.2 million, an 18.8% increase from $178.7 million

business_model.claim: End-market demand and order intake are driven by distributors' access to floor plan financing and end-users' costs of equipment ownership, including interest rates, insurance premiums, fuel prices affecting miles driven, and used-truck trade-in values.
quotes: Our independent distributor customers rely on floor plan financing in connection with the purchase of our products, and the availability of that financing on acceptable terms has a direct effect on the volume of their purchases.
This global rise in fuel costs has resulted in fewer miles driven which has, and may continue to, adversely impact the demand for our products.

Continuing increases in fuel costs, insurance premiums, and elevated interest rates have added cost pressures to our end-users, and fluctuations in the value of used trucks have affected trade-in values and new equipment purchases.

business_model.claim: State near-zero emission standards that limit diesel-powered commercial vehicle registrations restrict the number of vehicles sold in adopting states and negatively affected customer demand in 2024 and through the third quarter of 2025.
quotes: In recent years, regulations with near zero emission standards were adopted by certain states, which limit the amount of diesel-powered commercial vehicles that can be registered and, therefore, the number of vehicles we can sell in these states.
Compliance with these regulations negatively impacted customer demand during 2024 and through the third quarter of 2025 and were expected to continue to negatively impact customer demand.

business_model.claim: Pricing actions also move revenue, as the company rolled a prior cost-offsetting surcharge into its standard pricing structure and implemented a 3% price increase on domestic manufactured products.
quotes: We implemented a surcharge in April 2025 to partially offset these pressures; however, continued cost increases have exceeded the coverage provided by that surcharge.
As a result, in May 2026, we announced that the existing surcharge would be rolled into our standard pricing structure.
In addition, we announced a 3% price increase on all domestic manufactured products, which went into effect on all domestic manufactured products invoiced after July 31, 2026.

business_model.claim: Revenue and gross margin are influenced by the mix between manufactured units and third-party chassis, with a higher share of units lifting gross margin from 13.6% in 2024 to 15.2% in 2025, while chassis supplier production challenges can constrain quarterly output.
quotes: Gross profit as a percentage of sales was 15.2% for fiscal 2025 compared to 13.6% in fiscal 2024, an increase of 12.2%.
The increase was primarily due to a favorable product mix, which shifted from a higher percentage of chassis delivered throughout 2024 to a higher percentage of units throughout 2025.
For the full year, gross margins are now expected to be approximately 14%, higher than previously anticipated, reflecting a lower mix of chassis.

While the quarter was impacted by planned holiday downtime and production challenges among our chassis suppliers, the underlying strength in demand for our products gives us confidence as we move into the final quarter of 2026, and into 2027.

business_model.basis: stated in P1, P2, and P3
business_model.claim: Cost of operations is driven by direct materials—chiefly sheet steel, aluminum, and third-party components including hydraulic cylinders, winches, valves, pumps, and chassis—along with manufacturing labor, overhead, physical inventory adjustments, and inbound and outbound freight.
quotes: Cost of operations includes the direct cost of manufacturing, including direct materials, labor and related overhead, physical inventory adjustments, as well as inbound and outbound freight.
The manufacturing process for our products consists primarily of cutting and bending sheet steel or aluminum into parts that are welded together to form the wrecker, car carrier body, or trailer.

After the frame is formed, components such as hydraulic cylinders, winches, valves, and pumps that are purchased by us from third-party suppliers, are attached to the frame to form the completed wrecker or car carrier body.
We are dependent upon outside suppliers for our raw material needs, other purchased component parts, and chassis.

business_model.claim: Because Miller Industries has no long-term supply contracts, its input costs fluctuate with supplier price adjustments and trade tariffs, especially tariffs on specialty steel and aluminum.
quotes: Although we have no long-term supply contracts, management believes we have good relationships with our primary suppliers.
Some of our suppliers have implemented pricing adjustments and passed through tariff-related cost increases in response to changes in U.S and foreign trade policies over the last year.

While we believe the diversity and strength of our supply chain leaves us well-positioned to navigate these uncertainties, we expect tariffs, in particular on specialty steel and aluminum, will continue to adversely impact the Company’s operating results.

business_model.claim: Logistics disruptions, fuel price surges following hostilities affecting the Strait of Hormuz (through which approximately 20% of global oil and gas is transported), and European energy costs drive freight, petroleum-related material, and plant operating expenses.
quotes: In recent years, logistic disruptions and supplier shortages have caused delays in shipping and freight cost increases.

Most recently, the price of fuel surged in March 2026, after U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran, and retaliatory strikes by Iran on, among others, Israel, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, and international shipping vessels in the Strait of Hormuz, through which approximately 20% of the world’s oil and gas is transported.

In Europe, rising energy costs as a result of supply disruptions and increased winter demand for heating could place strain on our operations and our suppliers’ ability to maintain current production levels.

business_model.claim: Skilled manufacturing labor wages and retention costs are an ongoing cost driver, which management partially addressed in the third quarter of 2025 by reducing headcount by approximately 150 positions across three U.S. facilities.
quotes: The timely manufacture and delivery of our products requires an adequate supply of skilled labor, and the operating costs of our manufacturing facilities can be adversely affected by increasing labor costs in skilled positions.
In recent years we have experienced substantial increases in employee wages in order to retain and recruit a talented workforce.
Under this plan, we reduced our headcount by approximately 150 positions across three of our U.S. manufacturing facilities during the third quarter of 2025.

business_model.claim: Selling, general and administrative expenses ($89.0 million in 2025, up 3.1% from $86.3 million in 2024) are driven by territory sales representative commissions, workforce and executive RSU compensation, Omars acquisition and operating expenses, and a $2.7 million net impact from a 2025 enhanced retirement program.
quotes: Sales representatives receive commissions on direct sales based on product type and brand and generally are assigned specific territories in which to promote sales of our products and to maintain customer relationships.
Selling, general and administrative expenses in fiscal 2025 were $89.0 million compared to $86.3 million in fiscal 2024, an increase of 3.1%.
The net financial impact totaled $2.7 million.

business_model.claim: Net interest expense is driven by floor plan costs tied to sales volume and variable-rate credit facility borrowings (offset by interest billed on open customer receivables), while foreign sales and European subsidiary expenses create exposure to British pound sterling and euro exchange rate fluctuations.
quotes: The decrease in interest expense was primarily related to reduced floor plan costs associated with lower sales volume and decreased debt levels.
The increase in interest income was due to increased interest billings on open accounts receivable balances from customers.

In addition, a portion of our net sales derived outside the United States, as well as salaries of employees located outside the United States and certain other expenses, are denominated in foreign currencies, including the British pound sterling and the euro.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1 Business as management's description of the company and brand portfolio.
competitive_position.claim: Miller Industries describes itself as The World’s Largest Manufacturer of Towing and Recovery Equipment® and markets its products under 11 separate brand names.
quotes: Miller Industries, Inc., a Tennessee corporation, is The World’s Largest Manufacturer of Towing and Recovery Equipment®, with executive offices in Ooltewah, Tennessee, domestic manufacturing operations in Tennessee and Pennsylvania, and foreign manufacturing operations in France, the United Kingdom and, most recently, Italy.
We manufacture and market our car carriers, wreckers, and trailers under 11 separate brand names.

competitive_position.basis: Stated as management's belief in both the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1 Business and Q3 2026 Form 10-Q MD&A.
competitive_position.claim: Management identifies the strength of its distribution network and the breadth and quality of its product offerings as two key advantages over competitors.
quotes: Management believes the strength of our distribution network and the breadth and quality of our product offerings are two key advantages over our competitors.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1 Business under Competition.
competitive_position.claim: The company competes primarily on product quality, reputation, innovation, and customer service rather than solely on price, targeting professional towing operators.
quotes: We compete on many levels, including product quality and innovation, reputation, technology, customer service, product availability, and price, with an emphasis on product quality, innovation, and customer service.

Our marketing strategy is to continue to compete primarily on the basis of quality and reputation rather than solely on the basis of price, and to continue to target the growing group of professional towing operators who recognize the quality of our products.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1 Business; the >90 percent figure is explicitly described as management's belief.
competitive_position.claim: Its products are sold through approximately 76 distributor locations in North America and over 30 distributors in other foreign markets, with management estimating that more than 90 percent of independent distributors do not offer competing brands.
quotes: We sell our products to a diverse network of independent distributors, consisting of approximately 76 distributor locations in North America, that serve all 50 states, Canada and Mexico, and over 30 distributors that serve other foreign markets.

While most of our distributor agreements do not generally contain exclusivity provisions, management believes that more than 90 percent of our independent distributors do not offer products of any other towing and recovery equipment manufacturer, which we believe is a testament of their loyalty to our brands.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1 Business under Customers.
competitive_position.claim: No single distributor accounted for more than 10% of consolidated total sales in 2025, limiting dependence on any individual customer.
quotes: In 2025, no distributor accounted for more than 10% of our consolidated total sales and we do not consider our business to be materially dependent on any single customer.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1 Business.
competitive_position.claim: The company holds flagship brand positions across Century® and Jige™ and expanded its European manufacturing and distribution footprint in fiscal 2025 by acquiring Italy-based Omars – S.p.A.
quotes: The Century® brand is our “top-of-the-line” brand and represents what management believes to be the broadest product line in the industry.

Jige™ is a market leader best known for its innovative designs of car carriers and light-duty wreckers necessary to operate within the narrow confines of European cities, as well as heavy-duty wreckers.
With a highly complementary product portfolio, management believes this acquisition will expand Miller Industries’ footprint in the European market with an additional, well-recognized European brand.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1 Business and Q3 2026 Form 8-K Exhibit 99.1.
competitive_position.claim: Product differentiation is supported by a 53-engineer department, a Chattanooga R&D facility, the patented Raptor™ Control System, and the recent introduction of a 65-ton rotator.
quotes: Our manufacturing personnel, in consultation with our engineering department (which consists of 53 engineers), use sophisticated computer-aided design and stress analysis systems to test new product designs and integrate various product improvements.

The Century® M100 also features our patented Raptor™ Control System which includes wrecker controls that allow the boom to be remotely extended away from the vehicle to enhance operator sightlines during use and an information screen with load-sensing functions.
Continuing to innovate the Company’s product line; recently introduced the new 65-ton rotator (the Century M65) at an event attended by more than 1,000 global distributors and customers.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1 Business and Q3 2026 Form 8-K Exhibit 99.1.
competitive_position.claim: The company operates manufacturing facilities in the United States, France, Italy, and the United Kingdom, strengthened hydraulic-cylinder supply stability via its Southern Hydraulic Cylinder acquisition, and began an approximately $100 million Ooltewah expansion to support heavy-duty exports and military commitments exceeding $200 million.
quotes: The operations of SHC align with those of the Company, which has enhanced the stability of the Company’s supply chain since the acquisition.

To support future growth, European demand, and defense production commitments, Miller Industries previously announced the addition of a new 200,000+ sq ft facility at its Ooltewah headquarters site, at a cost of approximately $100 million.
Military commitments currently exceed $200 million, and additional global RFQs are underway.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1 Business under Customers.
competitive_position.claim: Miller Industries has been selected by the United States General Services Administration as an approved source for certain federal and defense agencies and sells to domestic and foreign governments through prime contractors.
quotes: Our products have been selected by the United States General Services Administration as an approved source for certain federal and defense agencies.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 7 MD&A and Q3 2026 Form 8-K Exhibit 99.1.
competitive_position.claim: Third-quarter 2026 revenue rebounded 18.8% year-over-year to $212.2 million after fiscal 2025 net sales fell 37.2% when the company reduced production to clear distribution-channel inventory buildup.
quotes: Revenue: $212.2 million, an 18.8% increase from $178.7 million
The decrease in net sales was primarily driven by lower production levels to mitigate inventory buildup in our distribution channel.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1 Business and Item 1A Risk Factors.
competitive_position.claim: Relatively low capital requirements for entry into towing and recovery manufacturing expose the company to potential new industry entrants.
quotes: Capital requirements for entry into the towing and recovery manufacturing industry have been relatively low, which could result in an increase in the number of competitors entering the industry.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1 Business and Item 1A Risk Factors.
competitive_position.claim: Some competitors may possess substantially greater financial and other resources and offer more attractive dealer and retail customer financing alternatives.
quotes: Some of our competitors may have substantially greater financial and other resources and may provide more attractive dealer and retail customer financing alternatives than us.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1A Risk Factors and Q3 2026 Form 10-Q Item 2 MD&A.
competitive_position.claim: New equipment sales also face competition from the market for used towing and recovery equipment, with used-truck value fluctuations affecting trade-in values and new purchases.
quotes: Competition for sales also comes from the market for used towing and recovery equipment.

Continuing increases in fuel costs, insurance premiums, and elevated interest rates have added cost pressures to our end-users, and fluctuations in the value of used trucks have affected trade-in values and new equipment purchases.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1A Risk Factors.
competitive_position.claim: Dependence on independent distributors outside the company's control means dealer missteps or contract terminations could damage brand reputation, pricing positions, and demand.
quotes: Because we depend on the pull-through demand generated by end-users for our products, any actions by the independent distributors, which are not in our control, may harm our reputation and damage the brand loyalty among our customer base.
In addition, if a significant number of independent dealers were to terminate their contracts, it could adversely impact our business, results of operations and financial condition.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1A Risk Factors and Q3 2026 Form 8-K Exhibit 99.1.
competitive_position.claim: Reliance on third-party suppliers for chassis, component parts, steel, and aluminum creates delivery-delay and shortage risks that could prompt customers to seek alternative solutions.
quotes: Delays in deliveries of our finished products due to delays of purchased component parts and chassis used in our products could also adversely affect future demand for our products if our customers reduce their purchase levels with us and/or seek alternative solutions to meet their demand.

Shortages and price increases and/or delays or unexpected cadence or quantities in the deliveries of, our raw materials and purchased component parts, including chassis, have had, and could continue to have, a material adverse effect on our profitability, financial performance, competitive position and reputation.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1A Risk Factors and Q3 2026 Form 10-Q Item 2 MD&A.
competitive_position.claim: Tariff uncertainty—particularly on specialty steel and aluminum—and rising input and ownership costs threaten operating results and could reduce volumes if price increases cannot be passed on.
quotes: While we believe the diversity and strength of our supply chain leaves us well-positioned to navigate these uncertainties, we expect tariffs, in particular on specialty steel and aluminum, will continue to adversely impact the Company’s operating results.
While we have attempted to pass increased costs on to our customers in the past, there can be no assurances that we will be able to continue doing so in the future.

Sustained price increases, surcharges or price inflation (or inflation pressure generally), in turn, may lead to declines in volume, and while we seek to project tradeoffs between price increases, surcharges and inflation, on the one hand, and volume, on the other, there can be no assurance that our projections will prove to be accurate.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1A Risk Factors.
competitive_position.claim: Tight competition for skilled manufacturing labor risks higher wage costs and competitor recruitment of employees trained by the company.
quotes: We invest significant time and expense in training our employees, which increases their value to competitors who may seek to recruit them.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1A Risk Factors.
competitive_position.claim: Government and military contracting involves intense bidding competition, fixed-price cost-overrun exposure, strict technical compliance rules, and funding or cancellation discretion.
quotes: Our U.S. and other government business is subject to the following risks, among others: (i) this business is susceptible to decreases in government spending, which may reduce future revenues; (ii) most of our contracts with governmental entities through prime contractors are fixed-price contracts, and our actual costs on any of these contracts could exceed our projected costs; (iii) competition for the award of these contracts is intense, and we may not be successful in bidding on future contracts; and (iv) the products we sell to governmental entities are subject to highly technical requirements, and any failure to comply with these requirements could result in unanticipated retrofit costs, delayed acceptance of products, late or reduced payment, or cancellation of the contract.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1A Risk Factors.
competitive_position.claim: Ongoing growth via acquisitions, such as Omars, introduces integration, internal-control, customer-dissatisfaction, and goodwill impairment risks.
quotes: Customer dissatisfaction or performance problems with an acquired business, technology, service or product could also have a material adverse effect on our reputation and business.
